name: stri_sub_replace
title: Replace a substring and return the copy

origin.description: Replace substrings and return the new character vector. This is the pipe-friendly form of stri_sub<-.

arguments.text: Arguments passed to stri_sub<-: str, from, to, length, omit_na, and use_matrix.

arguments.name: replacement
arguments.text: Replacement strings. Used when value is omitted.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: Replacement strings. When both are passed, value is written.

origin.details: The call is stri_sub<-. length wins over to. A negative length leaves the string unchanged. A start past the end appends, and from past to inserts at from. omit_na keeps the original string when an index or the replacement is missing.
origin.value: A character vector of the replaced strings.
origin.example:
s <- c("spam, spam, bacon, and spam", "eggs and spam")
stri_sub_replace(s, 1, 4, replacement = "stringi")

translation.description: Replace substrings and return the new strings. This calls stri_sub_assign.

arguments.name: args
arguments.text: Positional arguments of stri_sub_assign: str, from_, to, and length.

arguments.name: replacement
arguments.text: Replacement strings. Used when value is omitted.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: Replacement strings. When both are passed, value is written.

arguments.name: kwargs
arguments.text: omit_na and use_matrix, passed through to stri_sub_assign.

translation.details: The replacement is the same as stri_sub<-. A negative length leaves the string unchanged. from_ = 0 with a positive length keeps the inclusive end from + length - 1.
translation.value: A list of the replaced strings.
translation.example:
from stringi.sub import stri_sub_replace
s = ["spam, spam, bacon, and spam", "eggs and spam"]
print(stri_sub_replace(s, 1, 4, replacement="stringi"))
